question: After a water outbreak, irritable bowel syndrome struck 36% of those who fell ill and 10% who did not. Extra cases per 1,000 ill?
move: Subtract what would have happened anyway before crediting a cause.
ask: What would have happened anyway, before I give credit to the cause I like?
trap: Blaming the outbreak for all 360 cases, ignoring the background rate.
hint: Some of those who fell ill would have developed the condition without any outbreak.
steps: Cases among 1,000 who fell ill: 36% of 1,000 = 360.
Cases expected anyway, at the rate in those who stayed well: 10% of 1,000 = 100.

diagram.caption: Of 100 who fell ill, 36 got IBS; 10 would have anyway, so 26 are extra.

reference: Marshall, Thabane, Garg et al., Incidence and epidemiology of irritable bowel syndrome after a large waterborne outbreak of bacterial dysentery, Gastroenterology, 2006
